## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/Users/brandontautuan/.agents/skills`
- `r1` = `/Users/brandontautuan/.codex/skills/.system`
- `r2` = `/Users/brandontautuan/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-bundled`
- `r3` = `/Users/brandontautuan/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote`
- `r4` = `/Users/brandontautuan/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/sites/1.1.2/skills`
- `r5` = `/Users/brandontautuan/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/work-pets/0.1.6/skills`
- `r6` = `/Users/brandontautuan/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-primary-runtime`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r1/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r1/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow. (file: r1/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r1/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r1/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
- browser:control-in-app-browser: Control the in-app Browser. Use to open, navigate, inspect, test, click, type, screenshot, or verify local targets such as localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, file://, the current in-app browser tab, and websites shown side by side inside Codex. (file: r2/browser/26.623.101652/skills/control-in-app-browser/SKILL.md)
- chrome:control-chrome: Control the user's Chrome browser for tasks that depend on existing Chrome state: tabs, logged-in sessions, or extensions. Prefer purpose-built connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available. (file: r2/chrome/26.623.101652/skills/control-chrome/SKILL.md)
- documents:documents: Create, edit, redline, and comment on `.docx`, Word, and Google Docs-targeted document artifacts inside the container, with a strict render-and-verify workflow. Use `render_docx.py` to generate page PNGs (and optional PDF) for visual QA, then iterate until layout is flawless before delivering the final document. (file: r6/documents/26.630.12135/skills/documents/SKILL.md)
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill. (file: r0/find-skills/SKILL.md)
- pdf:pdf: Read, create, inspect, render, and verify PDF files where visual layout matters. Use Poppler rendering plus Python tools such as reportlab, pdfplumber, and pypdf for generation and extraction. (file: r6/pdf/26.630.12135/skills/pdf/SKILL.md)
- plugin-management:plugin-management: Discover and suggest relevant plugins, inspect app permissions and dependencies, and manage plugin connections or removal. Use when the user asks about plugins or when a task would materially benefit from an external app, account, service, or data source that available tools cannot access. (file: r3/plugin-management/0.1.0/skills/plugin-management/SKILL.md)
- presentations:Presentations: Create or edit PowerPoint or Google Slides decks (file: r6/presentations/26.630.12135/skills/presentations/SKILL.md)
- sites:sites: Use Sites when the user wants a website built for them (including a landing page, portfolio, dashboard, portal, tracker, hub, game, event registration, or tool), requests changes to a website already built with Sites, wants to publish a website with Sites, or wants to manage Sites hosting. (file: r4/sites/SKILL.md)
- sites:sites-remix: Remix a Site built with the Sites plugin into a new Site. Use when the user has identified the source Site and asks to remix it. (file: r4/sites-remix/SKILL.md)
- spreadsheets:Spreadsheets: Use this skill when a user requests to create, modify, analyze, visualize, or work with spreadsheet files (`.xlsx`, `.xls`, `.csv`, `.tsv`) or Google Sheets-targeted spreadsheet artifacts with formulas, formatting, charts, tables, and recalculation. (file: r6/spreadsheets/26.630.12135/skills/spreadsheets/SKILL.md)
- template-creator:template-creator: Create or update a reusable personal Codex artifact-template skill. Use when the user invokes $template-creator or asks in natural language to create a template using, from, or based on an attached Word document, PowerPoint presentation, or Excel workbook, or explicitly asks to edit or update a passed artifact-template skill. Do not use for one-off artifact creation from an existing template. (file: r6/template-creator/26.630.12135/skills/template-creator/SKILL.md)
- work-pets:create-pet: Create, repair, validate, preview, upload, or activate an animated v2 pet in ChatGPT Work mode from a character idea, brand cue, or reference image. fn transition(pattern: &[u8], index: usize, byte: u8) -> Option<usize> {
    match pattern.get(index) {
        Some(b'*') => Some(index),
        Some(&literal) if literal == byte => Some(index + 1),
        _ => None,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{CompileError, CompiledRule, ConflictCheckError, find_conflict, glob_matches};

    fn rule(
        subdomain: Option<&str>,
        method: Option<&str>,
        path: Option<&str>,
        action: &str,
    ) -> CompiledRule {
        CompiledRule::new(method, "acme.com", subdomain, path, action.into()).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn wildcard_hosts_respect_boundaries_and_nested_subdomains() {
        let rule = rule(Some("*"), None, None, "payment.read");
        assert!(rule.matches("GET", "a.b.acme.com", "/"));
        assert!(!rule.matches("GET", "acme.com", "/"));
        assert!(!rule.matches("GET", "evilacme.com", "/"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn globs_match_zero_or_more_characters() {
        assert!(glob_matches("/v1/refunds/*", "/v1/refunds/"));
        assert!(glob_matches("/v1/*/x/*", "/v1/a/b/x/c"));
        assert!(!glob_matches("/v1/refunds/*", "/v1/refunds"));
        assert!(glob_matches("/**/**/**", "/a/b/c/d"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn specificity_is_lexicographic() {
        let exact_host = rule(Some("api"), None, Some("/v1/*"), "payment.read");
        let wildcard_host = rule(
            Some("*"),
            Some("GET"),
            Some("/v1/payments"),
            "payment.create",
        );
        assert!(exact_host.compare_specificity(&wildcard_host).is_gt());
        let exact_path = rule(Some("api"), None, Some("/v1/payments"), "payment.read");
        assert!(exact_path.compare_specificity(&exact_host).is_gt());
    }

    #[test]
    fn detects_equal_specificity_overlaps_only() {
        let conflicting = vec![
            rule(Some("api"), None, Some("/v1/*a*bc"), "payment.read"),
            rule(Some("api"), None, Some("/v1/*ab*c"), "payment.refund"),
        ];
        assert_eq!(find_conflict(&conflicting).unwrap(), Some((0, 1)));
        let ordered = vec![
            rule(Some("api"), None, Some("/v1/*"), "payment.read"),
            rule(Some("api"), None, Some("/v1/payments"), "payment.refund"),
        ];
        assert_eq!(find_conflict(&ordered).unwrap(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_overlap_checks_that_exceed_the_state_limit() {
        let pattern = format!("/{}", "*".repeat(1_000));
        let rules = vec![
            rule(Some("api"), None, Some(&pattern), "payment.read"),
            rule(Some("api"), None, Some(&pattern), "payment.refund"),
        ];
        assert!(matches!(
            find_conflict(&rules),
            Err(ConflictCheckError::TooComplex {
                first: 0,
                second: 1
            })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_configurations_that_exceed_the_pair_check_limit() {
        let rules = (0..448)
            .map(|_| rule(Some("api"), None, None, "payment.read"))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        assert!(matches!(
            find_conflict(&rules),
            Err(ConflictCheckError::TooComplex { .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn explicit_methods_win_only_after_host_and_path_ties() {
        let any_method = rule(Some("api"), None, Some("/v1/*"), "payment.read");
        let get = rule(Some("api"), Some("GET"), Some("/v1/*"), "payment.create");
        assert!(get.compare_specificity(&any_method).is_gt());
        assert!(get.matches("GET", "api.acme.com", "/v1/x"));
        // `matches` receives normalized method tokens from `classify`.
        assert!(!get.matches("get", "api.acme.com", "/v1/x"));
        assert!(!get.matches("POST", "api.acme.com", "/v1/x"));
        let lower = rule(Some("api"), Some("get"), Some("/v1/*"), "payment.create");
        assert_eq!(lower.method.as_deref(), Some("GET"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn compiled_rules_only_retain_known_action_classes() {
        assert!(matches!(
            CompiledRule::new(None, "acme.com", None, None, "unknown.class".into()),
            Err(CompileError::ActionClass(_))
        ));
    }
}
# HARDENING.md — steering for the coding agent

Read this after `README.md`, `agents.md` and `Arch.md`. It turns the security
audit of `b2d8402` (see `backlog.md`) into ordered, bounded work items.

Precedence stays the same: README > fixed API > `agents.md` > `Arch.md` > this
file. If an item here conflicts with the README, stop and flag it.

## Ground rules

1. **Follow the design; only extend it where a defect was demonstrated.** Every
   item below either brings the code back in line with `Arch.md` (Tier 1), or
   adds to the design to close a reproduced problem (Tier 2/3). Do not
   restructure modules, add indexing, add dependencies, or "optimize" beyond
   what an item asks for. A linear scan is the accepted design (Arch §15).
2. **One item per commit.** Each commit contains the code change, a test that
   would have failed before it, and the matching `Arch.md` / `agents.md` edit.
   Code and docs must never disagree at any commit. The commit message names
   the item number (e.g. `H6: total conflict-analysis budget`).
3. **Never weaken a test to make it pass.** Never write a test that asserts the
   *less* sensitive class for an alternate spelling of a request. If a test
   seems wrong, stop and report rather than editing the expectation.
4. **Fail closed.** When unsure, the request is unclassified (`None`) or the
   config is rejected with an explicit `LoadError`. Never pick a class by
   guessing.
5. **Don't flip-flop on policy.** The policies in `Arch.md` §7/§9/§11 are
   decided. Do not revert method folding, `//` rejection, multi-label
   subdomains, or linear dot-segment removal.
6. **Same canonicalization both sides.** Any new path or host rule goes in the
   shared helpers in `normalize.rs` and applies to both config patterns and
   requests, unless the item says otherwise.
7. **Gates on every commit**, run from `Firma_take_home/`:
   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo build
   cargo test
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   ```
   The four tests in `tests/example.rs` must pass unchanged.
8. No `unwrap`/`expect` on untrusted input. `classify` must never panic. Keep
   `Classifier` `Send + Sync` and immutable after `load`.

## Work order

Do the items in this order. Stop after each tier and report.

---

## Tier 1 — make the code match the design

### H1. Check trailing slashes in one direction only (open HIGH, Audit 4/6)

- **Problem:** `classify` also checks `/x` against `/x/`. A narrower rule under
  a broader wildcard can never match: with `/v1/*/send` →
  `communication.external.send` and `/v1/*` → `payment.read`,
  `GET api.acme.com/v1/msg/send` returns `None`. This breaks README "the most
  specific wins".
- **Change (`src/lib.rs` `classify`):** only when the normalized path ends in
  `/` and isn't `/`, classify the path without that slash as well. Return
  `None` only if that result is `Some` and differs. A path without a trailing
  slash gets no alternate check.
- **Rationale for the doc:** the risk is a server stripping a trailing slash
  and running a more sensitive handler than the one classified. A request sent
  without the slash is already classified as sent.
- **Tests:**
  - `tests/classification.rs` `most_specific_rule_wins`: `/v1/msg/send` →
    `Some("communication.external.send")`.
  - `tests/security.rs`: `POST /v1/payouts` → `Some("payment.create")`, and
    `POST /v1/payouts/` → `None`.
  - Rename the security test to match the one-directional behaviour.
- **Docs:** Arch §9 and agents.md "Paths" say the check goes one way, with the
  rationale above.

### H2. Reject IP-like hosts (Arch §7, §9)

- **Problem:** only dotted-quad IPv4 is rejected. `010.0.0.1` and `127.1` load
  as config hosts and are accepted as request hosts.
- **Change (`normalize::host`):** reject any host whose last label is all
  digits. No real TLD is all-numeric (RFC 3696 §2). Config uses the same
  helper, so both sides are covered.
- **Tests:** a config `host` of `127.1` or `010.0.0.1` is rejected. A request
  host of `127.1`, `010.0.0.1` or `1.2.3.4.5` gives `None`.

### H3. Store the action class as `&'static str` (Arch §8)

- **Change:** `CompiledRule::action_class` holds the matching `ACTION_CLASSES`
  entry, found at compile time. An unknown class is a `CompileError`, which
  `load` maps to `SetError::UnknownActionClass`. `best_match` returns the
  stored reference.
- **Why:** only the seven classes can come back, guaranteed by the type rather
  than by validation order.

### H4. Make the robustness tests reach the matcher (Arch §17)

- **Problem:** the generator's alphabet doesn't contain `c`, `m` or `e`, so no
  generated host is ever under `acme.com`. Both tests only ever compare `None`
  with `None`.
- **Change (`tests/robustness.rs`):**
  - Pick the method from {`GET`, `POST`, `DELETE`, `get`, generated junk}.
  - Pick the host from {`api.acme.com`, `x.acme.com`, `a.b.acme.com`,
    `acme.com`, generated junk}.
  - Build the path from valid segments (`v1`, `refunds`, `x`, `.`, `..`,
    `%72efunds`, an empty last segment), then randomly mutate one byte.
- **Asserts:**
  - Results are deterministic and independent of set order.
  - Every result is `None` or a member of `ACTION_CLASSES`.
  - At least 25% of iterations classify to `Some`, so the test fails if the
    generator stops reaching the matcher again.
  - Use no new dependencies.

### H5. Test cleanups

- `tests/conflicts.rs` `same_class_duplicates_are_harmless`: change the path
  back from `/x*` to `/x`.
- `tests/security.rs` `method_case_does_not_fall_through_to_method_less_rule`:
  remove the standalone `DELETE` assertion that the loop already covers.
- `tests/conflicts.rs:165`: remove the stale "Exact subdomains are one DNS
  label" comment.

---

## Tier 2 — hardening that adds to the design

### H6. Bound the cost of conflict analysis by total work, not pair count (MED)

- **Problem:**
  - The 1M-state cap per pair multiplies across up to 100k pairs. 40 wildcard
    rules (a 42 KB config) take 21.6 s to load in release.
  - The pair cap counts *every* pair, so 448 rules on unrelated hosts fail with
    a misleading `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex` that names unrelated rules.
- **Change (`src/matcher.rs`, `src/config.rs`):**
  1. **Pattern length limit:** reject config `path` patterns longer than
     1024 bytes after normalization (`SetError::InvalidRule`, field `path`).
  2. **Total budget:** replace `MAX_CONFLICT_PAIR_CHECKS` with one total
     budget of glob-overlap states for the whole load (e.g. 4,000,000).
     Charge it only for pairs that reach `globs_overlap`, i.e. different
     class, equal specificity, and overlapping method and host. Cheap pairs
     cost nothing.
  3. **Short-circuit identical patterns:** before any budget check, two equal
     patterns (or both `None`) count as overlapping, so identical rules report
     `ConflictingRules`, not "too complex".
  4. **Rule-count limit:** add an explicit limit on total rules (e.g. 10,000)
     with its own `LoadError` variant, so the n² pair loop stays bounded.
- **Tests:**
  - 1,000 rules on 1,000 different hosts load.
  - 600 same-class exact paths in one set load.
  - The 40-rule adversarial config is rejected (too complex) or loads in under
    1 s in a debug build.
  - Two identical 1,000-`*` patterns with different classes give
    `ConflictingRules`.
  - A 1,025-byte pattern is rejected.
- **Docs:** Arch §13, §14 (list every `LoadError` variant) and §16 (state the
  limits and why).

### H7. Leave paths containing `;` unclassified (HIGH)

- **Problem:** `POST /v1/refunds;jsessionid=x/re_1` gives `payment.read`.
  Tomcat, Jetty and Spring strip `;` path parameters and run the refund.
- **Change:** reject a literal `;` in `normalize_path`, which covers both
  requests and patterns. `%3B` stays an encoded literal and is still accepted.
- **Tests (`tests/security.rs`):** `/v1/refunds;x/re_1` and
  `/v1/refunds;/re_1` give `None`. A config pattern containing `;` is
  rejected.
- **Docs:** add `;` to the rejected-forms list in Arch §7/§9 and agents.md
  "Paths", with the reason (servers strip path parameters).

### H8. Wildcard host rules: deeper base wins; no single-label base hosts (MED)

- **Problem:** a set with `host = "com"`, `subdomain = "*"`, `path = "/v1/*"`
  → `llm.inference` overrides Stripe's `*` rule on `stripe.com`.
  `POST api.stripe.com/v1/refunds/x` gives `llm.inference`, which breaks
  README "no precedence".
- **Change:**
  1. **Ranking:** in `Specificity`, put host *kind* (exact/bare beats wildcard)
     first, then base-host label count, before any path field. Exact and bare
     hosts use their full label count; they only overlap when the host strings
     are equal, so it doesn't change their ordering.
  2. **Config check:** reject a config `host` with fewer than two labels
     (`InvalidField("host")`).
- **Tests:**
  - With the Stripe set and a `co.uk`-style broad set loaded together,
    Stripe's rule wins for `api.stripe.com`.
  - `host = "com"` is rejected.
  - The existing tests that two wildcard rules on bases at the same depth
    conflict still pass.
- **Docs:** Arch §11 and agents.md "Specificity" add base depth after host
  kind. Arch §7 says the base host needs at least two labels.

### H9. Cap input sizes (LOW)

- **Change:**
  - A request `path` input longer than 8 KiB, measured before stripping the
    query, gives `None`.
  - A method longer than 32 bytes gives `None`.
  - Hosts are already bounded by the DNS length check.
- **Tests:** an 8,193-byte path gives `None`. An 8,192-byte valid path still
  classifies.
- **Docs:** Arch §9 and §16.

### H10. Reject confusing config values (LOW)

- `method = "*"` gives `InvalidRule { field: "method" }`. Someone might read it
  as "any method"; omitting `method` is how to say that.
- A config path with a `.` or `..` segment is rejected, whether or not it
  contains a wildcard. Today `/v1/../admin` is silently rewritten to `/admin`,
  which Arch §7 forbids ("no silent correction").
- Docs: Arch §7.

### H11. Error detail and doc sync (LOW)

- Add the rejected value to `SetError::InvalidRule` (e.g.
  `value: String`, Debug-quoted in the message).
- Arch §14:
  - List every variant that exists, including `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex` and
    the new limits.
  - Say that set and rule indexes are 0-based, and make the example messages
    match the real `Display` output.
- Arch §5: list `tests/robustness.rs`, and say config tests live in
  `src/config.rs` rather than `tests/config_validation.rs`.

`load()` must support multiple TOML mapping sets in the same call.

Example:

```rust
let classifier = load(&[
    payments_mapping,
    github_mapping,
    llm_mapping,
]).await?;
```

Requirements:

- Parse each set independently.
- Validate each set independently.
- Compile all accepted rules into a shared collection.
- Detect conflicts within and across mapping sets.
- Reject invalid combinations before exposing the classifier.
- Never give a mapping set priority because it was loaded first.
- Treat duplicate equivalent rules returning the same action class as harmless; they may be deduplicated.

A change in the ordering of mapping sets must not change classification results.

### 13. Conflict detection

Conflict detection happens during `load()`.

A conflict occurs when two rules:

1. Can match at least one identical valid HTTP request.
2. Have the same specificity for that request.
3. Return different action classes.

Example:

```toml
method = "POST"
path = "/v1/refunds/*"
action_class = "payment.refund"
```

versus:

```toml
method = "POST"
path = "/v1/refunds/*"
action_class = "payment.read"
```

Reject the combined configuration.

Conflicts are not limited to identical rule strings.

For example, two different wildcard patterns may overlap and have equal specificity.

The matcher module should provide shared primitives for:

- Checking whether two host matchers can overlap.
- Checking whether two method matchers can overlap.
- Checking whether two path patterns can overlap.
- Comparing rule specificity.

The configuration loader should call these primitives rather than implement its own matching semantics.

A conservative conflict detector must not silently accept an unresolved ambiguity. If exact overlap checking is not implemented for a supported pattern type, either restrict that pattern type during validation or reject potentially conflicting patterns with an explicit error.

Avoid silently selecting the first encountered rule.

### 14. Structured error handling

Replace the placeholder `LoadError`.

Use a `thiserror`-based enum with variants corresponding to major failure categories.

Suggested categories:

- Invalid TOML.
- Unsupported format version.
- Missing or empty required value.
- Invalid hostname.
- Invalid method.
- Invalid subdomain.
- Invalid path pattern.
- Invalid action class.
- Empty rule set.
- Conflicting rules.
- Unsupported or ambiguous configuration.

Every error should identify the relevant mapping set by input index and, when available, its declared name.


More elaborate indexing should only be introduced if benchmarks demonstrate a benefit.

### 16. Concurrency and performance

The library will be used inside HTTP handlers.

Requirements:

- `Classifier` must be `Send + Sync`.
- Rules remain immutable after loading.
- No locks should be necessary for ordinary classification.
- Avoid expensive preprocessing on every request.
- Precompute specificity metadata during loading.
- Compile path wildcard representations during loading.
- Keep classification deterministic under concurrent requests.
- Avoid unnecessary allocations where practical.

The public functions remain asynchronous because the starter API requires it, but internal parsing and matching do not require asynchronous tasks.

If practical, verify concurrent classifications through a Tokio test using a shared `Arc<Classifier>`.

### 17. Testing strategy

#### Configuration parsing tests

Cover:

- Valid mapping files.
- Invalid TOML syntax.
- Unknown top-level keys.
- Unknown rule-level keys.
- Missing required fields.
- Empty required strings.
- Unsupported format versions.
- Optional fields omitted.
- Empty rules.
- Invalid action classes.
- Malformed methods.
- Malformed hostnames.
- Invalid subdomains.
- Invalid paths.

#### Matching tests

Cover:

- Exact host matching.
- Bare hosts.
- Exact subdomains.
- Wildcard subdomains.
//! Parsing and validation for mapping-set TOML documents.

use serde::Deserialize;

use crate::{ACTION_CLASSES, SetError, normalize};

const MAX_PATTERN_BYTES: usize = 1_024;

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub(crate) struct MappingSet {
    pub(crate) format_version: u32,
    pub(crate) name: String,
    pub(crate) description: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) host: String,
    pub(crate) rules: Vec<Rule>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub(crate) struct Rule {
    pub(crate) method: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) subdomain: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) path: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) action_class: String,
}

/// Converts one TOML document to a checked mapping set. Errors carry the
/// set's declared name when the document parsed far enough to have one.
pub(crate) fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<MappingSet, (Option<String>, SetError)> {
    let set: MappingSet = toml::from_str(input).map_err(|error| (None, SetError::Toml(error)))?;
    match validate(&set) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(set),
        Err(error) => Err((Some(set.name), error)),
    }
}

fn validate(set: &MappingSet) -> Result<(), SetError> {
    if set.format_version != 1 {
        return Err(SetError::UnsupportedFormatVersion(set.format_version));
    }
    required_text("name", &set.name)?;
    if set
        .description
        .as_deref()
        .is_some_and(|description| description.chars().any(char::is_control))
    {
        return Err(SetError::InvalidField("description"));
    }
    validate_host(&set.host)?;
    if set.rules.is_empty() {
        return Err(SetError::InvalidField("rules"));
    }

    for (index, rule) in set.rules.iter().enumerate() {
        if !ACTION_CLASSES.contains(&rule.action_class.as_str()) {
            return Err(SetError::UnknownActionClass {
                rule: index,
                action_class: rule.action_class.clone(),
            });
        }
        if let Some(method) = &rule.method
            && normalize::method(method).is_none()
        {
            return Err(SetError::InvalidRule {
                rule: index,
                field: "method",
            });
        }
        if let Some(subdomain) = &rule.subdomain
            && subdomain != "*"
            && (!is_dns_name(subdomain) || normalize::host(subdomain).is_none())
        {
            return Err(SetError::InvalidRule {
                rule: index,
                field: "subdomain",
            });
        }
        if let Some(path) = &rule.path {
            let Some(normalized) = normalize::pattern_path(path) else {
                return Err(SetError::InvalidRule {
                    rule: index,
                    field: "path",
                });
            };
            if normalized.len() > MAX_PATTERN_BYTES {
                return Err(SetError::InvalidRule {
                    rule: index,
                    field: "path",
                });
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn required_text(field: &'static str, value: &str) -> Result<(), SetError> {
    if value.trim().is_empty() || value.chars().any(char::is_control) {
        Err(SetError::InvalidField(field))
    } else {
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn validate_host(host: &str) -> Result<(), SetError> {
    // Mapping hosts name an origin, not an HTTP authority. Ports and trailing
    // dots are accepted for request authorities but create duplicate mapping
    // identities, so reject them here.
    if !host.contains(':')
        && !host.ends_with('.')
        && normalize::host(host).is_some()
        && is_dns_name(host)
    {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(SetError::InvalidField("host"))
    }
}

fn is_dns_name(value: &str) -> bool {
    !value.is_empty() && value.len() <= 253 && value.split('.').all(is_dns_label)
}

fn is_dns_label(value: &str) -> bool {
    !value.is_empty()
        && value.len() <= 63
        && !value.starts_with('-')
        && !value.ends_with('-')
        && value
            .bytes()
            .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || byte == b'-')
}

//! Load-time conflict detection and set-order independence.

use action_classifier::{LoadError, RuleLocation, SetError, load};

fn set(name: &str, host: &str, rules: &str) -> String {
    format!("format_version = 1\nname = {name:?}\ndescription = \"test\"\nhost = {host:?}\n{rules}")
}

fn rule(subdomain: Option<&str>, method: Option<&str>, path: Option<&str>, class: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::from("\n[[rules]]\n");
    for (key, value) in [("subdomain", subdomain), ("method", method), ("path", path)] {
        if let Some(value) = value {
            out.push_str(&format!("{key} = {value:?}\n"));
        }
    }
    out.push_str(&format!("action_class = {class:?}\n"));
    out
}

fn location(set: usize, name: &str, rule: usize) -> RuleLocation {
    RuleLocation {
        set,
        name: name.into(),
        rule,
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn identical_rules_with_different_classes_conflict_across_sets() {
    let a = set(
        "A",
        "acme.com",
        &rule(
            Some("api"),
            Some("POST"),
            Some("/v1/refunds/*"),
            "payment.refund",
        ),
    );
    let b = set(
        "B",
        "acme.com",
        &format!(
            "{}{}",
            rule(None, None, Some("/pricing"), "payment.read"),
            rule(
                Some("api"),
                Some("POST"),
                Some("/v1/refunds/*"),
                "payment.read"
            ),
        ),
    );
    match load(&[&a, &b]).await {
        Err(LoadError::ConflictingRules { first, second }) => {
            assert_eq!(first, location(0, "A", 0));
            assert_eq!(second, location(1, "B", 1));
        }
        other => panic!("expected conflict, got {:?}", other.err()),
    }
}

# HARDENING.md — steering for the coding agent

Read this after `README.md`, `agents.md` and `Arch.md`. It turns the security
audit of `b2d8402` (see `backlog.md`) into ordered, bounded work items.

Precedence stays the same: README > fixed API > `agents.md` > `Arch.md` > this
file. If an item here conflicts with the README, stop and flag it.

## Ground rules

1. **Follow the design; only extend it where a defect was demonstrated.** Every
   item below either brings the code back in line with `Arch.md` (Tier 1), or
   adds to the design to close a reproduced problem (Tier 2/3). Do not
   restructure modules, add indexing, add dependencies, or "optimize" beyond
   what an item asks for. A linear scan is the accepted design (Arch §15).
2. **One item per commit.** Each commit contains the code change, a test that
   would have failed before it, and the matching `Arch.md` / `agents.md` edit.
   Code and docs must never disagree at any commit. The commit message names
   the item number (e.g. `H6: total conflict-analysis budget`).
3. **Never weaken a test to make it pass.** Never write a test that asserts the
   *less* sensitive class for an alternate spelling of a request. If a test
   seems wrong, stop and report rather than editing the expectation.
4. **Fail closed.** When unsure, the request is unclassified (`None`) or the
   config is rejected with an explicit `LoadError`. Never pick a class by
   guessing.
5. **Don't flip-flop on policy.** The policies in `Arch.md` §7/§9/§11 are
   decided. Do not revert method folding, `//` rejection, multi-label
   subdomains, or linear dot-segment removal.
6. **Same canonicalization both sides.** Any new path or host rule goes in the
   shared helpers in `normalize.rs` and applies to both config patterns and
   requests, unless the item says otherwise.
7. **Gates on every commit**, run from `Firma_take_home/`:
   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo build
   cargo test
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   ```
   The four tests in `tests/example.rs` must pass unchanged.
8. No `unwrap`/`expect` on untrusted input. `classify` must never panic. Keep
   `Classifier` `Send + Sync` and immutable after `load`.

## Work order

Do the items in this order. Stop after each tier and report.

## Tier 1 — make the code match the design

### H1. Check trailing slashes in one direction only (open HIGH, Audit 4/6)

- **Problem:** `classify` also checks `/x` against `/x/`. A narrower rule under
  a broader wildcard can never match: with `/v1/*/send` →
  `communication.external.send` and `/v1/*` → `payment.read`,
  `GET api.acme.com/v1/msg/send` returns `None`. This breaks README "the most
  specific wins".
- **Change (`src/lib.rs` `classify`):** only when the normalized path ends in
  `/` and isn't `/`, classify the path without that slash as well. Return
  `None` only if that result is `Some` and differs. A path without a trailing
  slash gets no alternate check.
- **Rationale for the doc:** the risk is a server stripping a trailing slash
  and running a more sensitive handler than the one classified. A request sent
  without the slash is already classified as sent.
- **Tests:**
  - `tests/classification.rs` `most_specific_rule_wins`: `/v1/msg/send` →
    `Some("communication.external.send")`.
  - `tests/security.rs`: `POST /v1/payouts` → `Some("payment.create")`, and
    `POST /v1/payouts/` → `None`.
  - Rename the security test to match the one-directional behaviour.
- **Docs:** Arch §9 and agents.md "Paths" say the check goes one way, with the
  rationale above.

### H2. Reject IP-like hosts (Arch §7, §9)

- **Problem:** only dotted-quad IPv4 is rejected. `010.0.0.1` and `127.1` load
  as config hosts and are accepted as request hosts.
- **Change (`normalize::host`):** reject any host whose last label is all
  digits. No real TLD is all-numeric (RFC 3696 §2). Config uses the same
  helper, so both sides are covered.
- **Tests:** a config `host` of `127.1` or `010.0.0.1` is rejected. A request
  host of `127.1`, `010.0.0.1` or `1.2.3.4.5` gives `None`.

### H3. Store the action class as `&'static str` (Arch §8)

- **Change:** `CompiledRule::action_class` holds the matching `ACTION_CLASSES`
  entry, found at compile time. An unknown class is a `CompileError`, which
  `load` maps to `SetError::UnknownActionClass`. `best_match` returns the
  stored reference.
- **Why:** only the seven classes can come back, guaranteed by the type rather
  than by validation order.

### H4. Make the robustness tests reach the matcher (Arch §17)

- **Problem:** the generator's alphabet doesn't contain `c`, `m` or `e`, so no

- **Change (`tests/robustness.rs`):**

- **Asserts:**
  - Results are deterministic and independent of set order.
  - Every result is `None` or a member of `ACTION_CLASSES`.
  - At least 25% of iterations classify to `Some`, so the test fails if the
    generator stops reaching the matcher again.
  - Use no new dependencies.

- `tests/security.rs` `method_case_does_not_fall_through_to_method_less_rule`:

- `tests/conflicts.rs:165`: remove the stale "Exact subdomains are one DNS

## Tier 2 — hardening that adds to the design

### H6. Bound the cost of conflict analysis by total work, not pair count (MED)

- **Problem:**
  - The 1M-state cap per pair multiplies across up to 100k pairs. 40 wildcard
    rules (a 42 KB config) take 21.6 s to load in release.
  - The pair cap counts *every* pair, so 448 rules on unrelated hosts fail with
    a misleading `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex` that names unrelated rules.
- **Change (`src/matcher.rs`, `src/config.rs`):**
  1. **Pattern length limit:** reject config `path` patterns longer than
     1024 bytes after normalization (`SetError::InvalidRule`, field `path`).
  2. **Total budget:** replace `MAX_CONFLICT_PAIR_CHECKS` with one total
     budget of glob-overlap states for the whole load (e.g. 4,000,000).
     Charge it only for pairs that reach `globs_overlap`, i.e. different
     class, equal specificity, and overlapping method and host. Cheap pairs
     cost nothing.
  3. **Short-circuit identical patterns:** before any budget check, two equal
     patterns (or both `None`) count as overlapping, so identical rules report
     `ConflictingRules`, not "too complex".
  4. **Rule-count limit:** add an explicit limit on total rules (e.g. 10,000)
     with its own `LoadError` variant, so the n² pair loop stays bounded.
- **Tests:**
  - 1,000 rules on 1,000 different hosts load.
  - 600 same-class exact paths in one set load.
  - The 40-rule adversarial config is rejected (too complex) or loads in under
    1 s in a debug build.
  - Two identical 1,000-`*` patterns with different classes give
    `ConflictingRules`.
  - A 1,025-byte pattern is rejected.
- **Docs:** Arch §13, §14 (list every `LoadError` variant) and §16 (state the
  limits and why).

### H7. Leave paths containing `;` unclassified (HIGH)

- **Problem:** `POST /v1/refunds;jsessionid=x/re_1` gives `payment.read`.
  Tomcat, Jetty and Spring strip `;` path parameters and run the refund.
- **Change:** reject a literal `;` in `normalize_path`, which covers both
  requests and patterns. `%3B` stays an encoded literal and is still accepted.
- **Tests (`tests/security.rs`):** `/v1/refunds;x/re_1` and
  `/v1/refunds;/re_1` give `None`. A config pattern containing `;` is
  rejected.
- **Docs:** add `;` to the rejected-forms list in Arch §7/§9 and agents.md
  "Paths", with the reason (servers strip path parameters).

### H8. Wildcard host rules: deeper base wins; no single-label base hosts (MED)

- **Problem:** a set with `host = "com"`, `subdomain = "*"`, `path = "/v1/*"`
  → `llm.inference` overrides Stripe's `*` rule on `stripe.com`.
  `POST api.stripe.com/v1/refunds/x` gives `llm.inference`, which breaks
  README "no precedence".
- **Change:**
  1. **Ranking:** in `Specificity`, put host *kind* (exact/bare beats wildcard)
     first, then base-host label count, before any path field. Exact and bare
     hosts use their full label count; they only overlap when the host strings
     are equal, so it doesn't change their ordering.
  2. **Config check:** reject a config `host` with fewer than two labels
     (`InvalidField("host")`).
- **Tests:**
  - With the Stripe set and a `co.uk`-style broad set loaded together,
    Stripe's rule wins for `api.stripe.com`.
  - `host = "com"` is rejected.
  - The existing tests that two wildcard rules on bases at the same depth
    conflict still pass.
- **Docs:** Arch §11 and agents.md "Specificity" add base depth after host
  kind. Arch §7 says the base host needs at least two labels.

### H9. Cap input sizes (LOW)

- **Change:**
  - A request `path` input longer than 8 KiB, measured before stripping the
    query, gives `None`.
  - A method longer than 32 bytes gives `None`.
  - Hosts are already bounded by the DNS length check.
- **Tests:** an 8,193-byte path gives `None`. An 8,192-byte valid path still
  classifies.
- **Docs:** Arch §9 and §16.

### H10. Reject confusing config values (LOW)

- `method = "*"` gives `InvalidRule { field: "method" }`. Someone might read it
  as "any method"; omitting `method` is how to say that.
- A config path with a `.` or `..` segment is rejected, whether or not it
  contains a wildcard. Today `/v1/../admin` is silently rewritten to `/admin`,
  which Arch §7 forbids ("no silent correction").
- Docs: Arch §7.

### H11. Error detail and doc sync (LOW)

- Add the rejected value to `SetError::InvalidRule` (e.g.
  `value: String`, Debug-quoted in the message).
- Arch §14:
  - List every variant that exists, including `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex` and
    the new limits.
  - Say that set and rule indexes are 0-based, and make the example messages
    match the real `Display` output.
- Arch §5: list `tests/robustness.rs`, and say config tests live in

`load()` must support multiple TOML mapping sets in the same call.

Example:

```rust
let classifier = load(&[
    payments_mapping,
    github_mapping,
    llm_mapping,
]).await?;
```

Requirements:

- Parse each set independently.
- Validate each set independently.
- Compile all accepted rules into a shared collection.
- Detect conflicts within and across mapping sets.
- Reject invalid combinations before exposing the classifier.
- Never give a mapping set priority because it was loaded first.
- Treat duplicate equivalent rules returning the same action class as harmless; they may be deduplicated.

A change in the ordering of mapping sets must not change classification results.

### 13. Conflict detection

Conflict detection happens during `load()`.

A conflict occurs when two rules:

1. Can match at least one identical valid HTTP request.
2. Have the same specificity for that request.
3. Return different action classes.

Example:

```toml
method = "POST"
path = "/v1/refunds/*"
action_class = "payment.refund"
```

versus:

```toml
method = "POST"
path = "/v1/refunds/*"
action_class = "payment.read"
```

Reject the combined configuration.

Conflicts are not limited to identical rule strings.

For example, two different wildcard patterns may overlap and have equal specificity.

The matcher module should provide shared primitives for:

- Checking whether two host matchers can overlap.
- Checking whether two method matchers can overlap.
- Checking whether two path patterns can overlap.
- Comparing rule specificity.

The configuration loader should call these primitives rather than implement its own matching semantics.

A conservative conflict detector must not silently accept an unresolved ambiguity. If exact overlap checking is not implemented for a supported pattern type, either restrict that pattern type during validation or reject potentially conflicting patterns with an explicit error.

Avoid silently selecting the first encountered rule.

### 14. Structured error handling

Replace the placeholder `LoadError`.

Use a `thiserror`-based enum with variants corresponding to major failure categories.

Suggested categories:

- Invalid TOML.
- Unsupported format version.
- Missing or empty required value.
- Invalid hostname.
- Invalid method.
- Invalid subdomain.
- Invalid path pattern.
- Invalid action class.
- Empty rule set.
- Conflicting rules.
- Unsupported or ambiguous configuration.

Every error should identify the relevant mapping set by input index and, when available, its declared name.


More elaborate indexing should only be introduced if benchmarks demonstrate a benefit.

### 16. Concurrency and performance

The library will be used inside HTTP handlers.

Requirements:

- `Classifier` must be `Send + Sync`.
- Rules remain immutable after loading.
- No locks should be necessary for ordinary classification.
- Avoid expensive preprocessing on every request.
- Precompute specificity metadata during loading.
- Compile path wildcard representations during loading.
- Keep classification deterministic under concurrent requests.
- Avoid unnecessary allocations where practical.

The public functions remain asynchronous because the starter API requires it, but internal parsing and matching do not require asynchronous tasks.

If practical, verify concurrent classifications through a Tokio test using a shared `Arc<Classifier>`.

### 17. Testing strategy

#### Configuration parsing tests

Cover:

- Valid mapping files.
- Invalid TOML syntax.
- Unknown top-level keys.
- Unknown rule-level keys.
- Missing required fields.
- Empty required strings.
- Unsupported format versions.
- Optional fields omitted.
- Empty rules.
- Invalid action classes.
- Malformed methods.
- Malformed hostnames.
- Invalid subdomains.
- Invalid paths.

#### Matching tests

Cover:

- Exact host matching.
- Bare hosts.
- Exact subdomains.
- Wildcard subdomains.
//! Parsing and validation for mapping-set TOML documents.

use serde::Deserialize;

use crate::{ACTION_CLASSES, SetError, normalize};

const MAX_PATTERN_BYTES: usize = 1_024;

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub(crate) struct MappingSet {
    pub(crate) format_version: u32,
    pub(crate) name: String,
    pub(crate) description: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) host: String,
    pub(crate) rules: Vec<Rule>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub(crate) struct Rule {
    pub(crate) method: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) subdomain: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) path: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) action_class: String,
}

/// Converts one TOML document to a checked mapping set. Errors carry the
/// set's declared name when the document parsed far enough to have one.
pub(crate) fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<MappingSet, (Option<String>, SetError)> {
    let set: MappingSet = toml::from_str(input).map_err(|error| (None, SetError::Toml(error)))?;
    match validate(&set) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(set),
        Err(error) => Err((Some(set.name), error)),
    }
}

fn validate(set: &MappingSet) -> Result<(), SetError> {
    if set.format_version != 1 {
        return Err(SetError::UnsupportedFormatVersion(set.format_version));
    }
    required_text("name", &set.name)?;
    if set
        .description
        .as_deref()
        .is_some_and(|description| description.chars().any(char::is_control))
    {
        return Err(SetError::InvalidField("description"));
    }
    validate_host(&set.host)?;
    if set.rules.is_empty() {
        return Err(SetError::InvalidField("rules"));
    }

    for (index, rule) in set.rules.iter().enumerate() {
        if !ACTION_CLASSES.contains(&rule.action_class.as_str()) {
            return Err(SetError::UnknownActionClass {
                rule: index,
                action_class: rule.action_class.clone(),
            });
        }
        if let Some(method) = &rule.method
            && normalize::method(method).is_none()
        {
            return Err(SetError::InvalidRule {
                rule: index,
                field: "method",
            });
        }
        if let Some(subdomain) = &rule.subdomain
            && subdomain != "*"
            && (!is_dns_name(subdomain) || normalize::host(subdomain).is_none())
        {
            return Err(SetError::InvalidRule {
                rule: index,
                field: "subdomain",
            });
        }
        if let Some(path) = &rule.path {
            let Some(normalized) = normalize::pattern_path(path) else {
                return Err(SetError::InvalidRule {
                    rule: index,
                    field: "path",
                });
            };
            if normalized.len() > MAX_PATTERN_BYTES {
                return Err(SetError::InvalidRule {
                    rule: index,
                    field: "path",
                });
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn required_text(field: &'static str, value: &str) -> Result<(), SetError> {
    if value.trim().is_empty() || value.chars().any(char::is_control) {
        Err(SetError::InvalidField(field))
    } else {
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn validate_host(host: &str) -> Result<(), SetError> {
    // Mapping hosts name an origin, not an HTTP authority. Ports and trailing
    // dots are accepted for request authorities but create duplicate mapping
    // identities, so reject them here.
    if !host.contains(':')
        && !host.ends_with('.')
        && normalize::host(host).is_some()
        && is_dns_name(host)
    {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(SetError::InvalidField("host"))
    }
}

fn is_dns_name(value: &str) -> bool {
    !value.is_empty() && value.len() <= 253 && value.split('.').all(is_dns_label)
}

fn is_dns_label(value: &str) -> bool {
    !value.is_empty()
        && value.len() <= 63
        && !value.starts_with('-')
        && !value.ends_with('-')
        && value
            .bytes()
            .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || byte == b'-')
}

//! Load-time conflict detection and set-order independence.

use action_classifier::{LoadError, RuleLocation, SetError, load};

fn set(name: &str, host: &str, rules: &str) -> String {
    format!("format_version = 1\nname = {name:?}\ndescription = \"test\"\nhost = {host:?}\n{rules}")
}

fn rule(subdomain: Option<&str>, method: Option<&str>, path: Option<&str>, class: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::from("\n[[rules]]\n");
    for (key, value) in [("subdomain", subdomain), ("method", method), ("path", path)] {
        if let Some(value) = value {
            out.push_str(&format!("{key} = {value:?}\n"));
        }
    }
    out.push_str(&format!("action_class = {class:?}\n"));
    out
}

fn location(set: usize, name: &str, rule: usize) -> RuleLocation {
    RuleLocation {
        set,
        name: name.into(),
        rule,
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn identical_rules_with_different_classes_conflict_across_sets() {
    let a = set(
        "A",
        "acme.com",
        &rule(
            Some("api"),
            Some("POST"),
            Some("/v1/refunds/*"),
            "payment.refund",
        ),
    );
    let b = set(
        "B",
        "acme.com",
        &format!(
            "{}{}",
            rule(None, None, Some("/pricing"), "payment.read"),
            rule(
                Some("api"),
                Some("POST"),
                Some("/v1/refunds/*"),
                "payment.read"
            ),
        ),
    );
    match load(&[&a, &b]).await {
        Err(LoadError::ConflictingRules { first, second }) => {
            assert_eq!(first, location(0, "A", 0));
            assert_eq!(second, location(1, "B", 1));
        }
        other => panic!("expected conflict, got {:?}", other.err()),
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn conflict_message_names_both_rules() {
    let a = set("A", "acme.com", &rule(None, None, Some("/x"), "repo.read"));
    let b = set("B", "acme.com", &rule(None, None, Some("/x"), "repo.write"));
    let message = load(&[&a, &b]).await.err().unwrap().to_string();
    assert!(message.contains(r#"mapping set 0 "A" rule 0"#), "{message}");
    assert!(message.contains(r#"mapping set 1 "B" rule 0"#), "{message}");
}

Read this after `README.md`, `agents.md` and `Arch.md`. It turns the security
audit of `b2d8402` (see `backlog.md`) into ordered, bounded work items.

Precedence stays the same: README > fixed API > `agents.md` > `Arch.md` > this
file. If an item here conflicts with the README, stop and flag it.

## Ground rules

1. **Follow the design; only extend it where a defect was demonstrated.** Every
   item below either brings the code back in line with `Arch.md` (Tier 1), or
   adds to the design to close a reproduced problem (Tier 2/3). Do not
   restructure modules, add indexing, add dependencies, or "optimize" beyond
   what an item asks for. A linear scan is the accepted design (Arch §15).
2. **One item per commit.** Each commit contains the code change, a test that
   would have failed before it, and the matching `Arch.md` / `agents.md` edit.
   Code and docs must never disagree at any commit. The commit message names
   the item number (e.g. `H6: total conflict-analysis budget`).
3. **Never weaken a test to make it pass.** Never write a test that asserts the
   *less* sensitive class for an alternate spelling of a request. If a test
   seems wrong, stop and report rather than editing the expectation.
4. **Fail closed.** When unsure, the request is unclassified (`None`) or the
   config is rejected with an explicit `LoadError`. Never pick a class by

5. **Don't flip-flop on policy.** The policies in `Arch.md` §7/§9/§11 are
   decided. Do not revert method folding, `//` rejection, multi-label
   subdomains, or linear dot-segment removal.
6. **Same canonicalization both sides.** Any new path or host rule goes in the
   shared helpers in `normalize.rs` and applies to both config patterns and
   requests, unless the item says otherwise.
7. **Gates on every commit**, run from `Firma_take_home/`:
   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo build
   cargo test
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   ```
   The four tests in `tests/example.rs` must pass unchanged.
8. No `unwrap`/`expect` on untrusted input. `classify` must never panic. Keep
   `Classifier` `Send + Sync` and immutable after `load`.

## Work order

Do the items in this order. Stop after each tier and report.

## Tier 1 — make the code match the design

### H1. Check trailing slashes in one direction only (open HIGH, Audit 4/6)

- **Problem:** `classify` also checks `/x` against `/x/`. A narrower rule under
  a broader wildcard can never match: with `/v1/*/send` →
  `communication.external.send` and `/v1/*` → `payment.read`,
  `GET api.acme.com/v1/msg/send` returns `None`. This breaks README "the most
  specific wins".
- **Change (`src/lib.rs` `classify`):** only when the normalized path ends in
  `/` and isn't `/`, classify the path without that slash as well. Return
  `None` only if that result is `Some` and differs. A path without a trailing
  slash gets no alternate check.
- **Rationale for the doc:** the risk is a server stripping a trailing slash
  and running a more sensitive handler than the one classified. A request sent
  without the slash is already classified as sent.
- **Tests:**
  - `tests/classification.rs` `most_specific_rule_wins`: `/v1/msg/send` →
    `Some("communication.external.send")`.
  - `tests/security.rs`: `POST /v1/payouts` → `Some("payment.create")`, and
    `POST /v1/payouts/` → `None`.

- **Docs:** Arch §9 and agents.md "Paths" say the check goes one way, with the

### H2. Reject IP-like hosts (Arch §7, §9)

- **Problem:** only dotted-quad IPv4 is rejected. `010.0.0.1` and `127.1` load

- **Change (`normalize::host`):** reject any host whose last label is all

- **Tests:** a config `host` of `127.1` or `010.0.0.1` is rejected. A request

- **Change:** `CompiledRule::action_class` holds the matching `ACTION_CLASSES`

## Tier 2 — hardening that adds to the design

### H6. Bound the cost of conflict analysis by total work, not pair count (MED)

- **Problem:**
  - The 1M-state cap per pair multiplies across up to 100k pairs. 40 wildcard
    rules (a 42 KB config) take 21.6 s to load in release.
  - The pair cap counts *every* pair, so 448 rules on unrelated hosts fail with
    a misleading `ConflictAnalysisTooComplex` that names unrelated rules.
- **Change (`src/matcher.rs`, `src/config.rs`):**
  1. **Pattern length limit:** reject config `path` patterns longer than
     1024 bytes after normalization (`SetError::InvalidRule`, field `path`).
  2. **Total budget:** replace `MAX_CONFLICT_PAIR_CHECKS` with one total
     budget of glob-overlap states for the whole load (e.g. 4,000,000).
     Charge it only for pairs that reach `globs_overlap`, i.e. different
     class, equal specificity, and overlapping method and host. Cheap pairs
     cost nothing.
  3. **Short-circuit identical patterns:** before any budget check, two equal
     patterns (or both `None`) count as overlapping, so identical rules report
     `ConflictingRules`, not "too complex".
  4. **Rule-count limit:** add an explicit limit on total rules (e.g. 10,000)
     with its own `LoadError` variant, so the n² pair loop stays bounded.
- **Tests:**
  - 1,000 rules on 1,000 different hosts load.
  - 600 same-class exact paths in one set load.
  - The 40-rule adversarial config is rejected (too complex) or loads in under
    1 s in a debug build.
  - Two identical 1,000-`*` patterns with different classes give
    `ConflictingRules`.
  - A 1,025-byte pattern is rejected.
- **Docs:** Arch §13, §14 (list every `LoadError` variant) and §16 (state the
  limits and why).

### H7. Leave paths containing `;` unclassified (HIGH)

- **Problem:** `POST /v1/refunds;jsessionid=x/re_1` gives `payment.read`.
  Tomcat, Jetty and Spring strip `;` path parameters and run the refund.
- **Change:** reject a literal `;` in `normalize_path`, which covers both
  requests and patterns. `%3B` stays an encoded literal and is still accepted.
- **Tests (`tests/security.rs`):** `/v1/refunds;x/re_1` and
  `/v1/refunds;/re_1` give `None`. A config pattern containing `;` is
  rejected.
- **Docs:** add `;` to the rejected-forms list in Arch §7/§9 and agents.md
  "Paths", with the reason (servers strip path parameters).

### H8. Wildcard host rules: deeper base wins; no single-label base hosts (MED)

- **Problem:** a set with `host = "com"`, `subdomain = "*"`, `path = "/v1/*"`
  → `llm.inference` overrides Stripe's `*` rule on `stripe.com`.
  `POST api.stripe.com/v1/refunds/x` gives `llm.inference`, which breaks

- **Change:**
  1. **Ranking:** in `Specificity`, put host *kind* (exact/bare beats wildcard)

  - The existing tests that two wildcard rules on bases at the same depth

- **Docs:** Arch §11 and agents.md "Specificity" add base depth after host

- **Change:**

`load()` must support multiple TOML mapping sets in the same call.

Example:

```rust
let classifier = load(&[
    payments_mapping,
    github_mapping,
    llm_mapping,
]).await?;
```

Requirements:

- Parse each set independently.
- Validate each set independently.
- Compile all accepted rules into a shared collection.
- Detect conflicts within and across mapping sets.
- Reject invalid combinations before exposing the classifier.
- Never give a mapping set priority because it was loaded first.
- Treat duplicate equivalent rules returning the same action class as harmless; they may be deduplicated.

A change in the ordering of mapping sets must not change classification results.

### 13. Conflict detection

Conflict detection happens during `load()`.

A conflict occurs when two rules:

1. Can match at least one identical valid HTTP request.
2. Have the same specificity for that request.
3. Return different action classes.

Example:

```toml
method = "POST"
path = "/v1/refunds/*"
action_class = "payment.refund"
```

versus:

```toml
method = "POST"
path = "/v1/refunds/*"
action_class = "payment.read"
```

Reject the combined configuration.

Conflicts are not limited to identical rule strings.

For example, two different wildcard patterns may overlap and have equal specificity.

The matcher module should provide shared primitives for:

- Checking whether two host matchers can overlap.
- Checking whether two method matchers can overlap.
- Checking whether two path patterns can overlap.
- Comparing rule specificity.

The configuration loader should call these primitives rather than implement its own matching semantics.

A conservative conflict detector must not silently accept an unresolved ambiguity. If exact overlap checking is not implemented for a supported pattern type, either restrict that pattern type during validation or reject potentially conflicting patterns with an explicit error.

Avoid silently selecting the first encountered rule.

### 14. Structured error handling

Replace the placeholder `LoadError`.

Use a `thiserror`-based enum with variants corresponding to major failure categories.

Suggested categories:

- Invalid TOML.
- Unsupported format version.
- Missing or empty required value.
- Invalid hostname.
- Invalid method.
- Invalid subdomain.
- Invalid path pattern.
- Invalid action class.
- Empty rule set.
- Conflicting rules.
- Unsupported or ambiguous configuration.

Every error should identify the relevant mapping set by input index and, when available, its declared name.


More elaborate indexing should only be introduced if benchmarks demonstrate a benefit.

### 16. Concurrency and performance

The library will be used inside HTTP handlers.

Requirements:

- `Classifier` must be `Send + Sync`.
- Rules remain immutable after loading.
- No locks should be necessary for ordinary classification.
- Avoid expensive preprocessing on every request.
- Precompute specificity metadata during loading.
- Compile path wildcard representations during loading.
- Keep classification deterministic under concurrent requests.
- Avoid unnecessary allocations where practical.

The public functions remain asynchronous because the starter API requires it, but internal parsing and matching do not require asynchronous tasks.

If practical, verify concurrent classifications through a Tokio test using a shared `Arc<Classifier>`.

### 17. Testing strategy

#### Configuration parsing tests

Cover:

- Valid mapping files.
- Invalid TOML syntax.
- Unknown top-level keys.
- Unknown rule-level keys.
- Missing required fields.
- Empty required strings.
- Unsupported format versions.
- Optional fields omitted.
- Empty rules.
- Invalid action classes.
- Malformed methods.
- Malformed hostnames.
- Invalid subdomains.
- Invalid paths.

#### Matching tests

Cover:

- Exact host matching.
- Bare hosts.
- Exact subdomains.
- Wildcard subdomains.
//! Parsing and validation for mapping-set TOML documents.

use serde::Deserialize;

use crate::{ACTION_CLASSES, SetError, normalize};

const MAX_PATTERN_BYTES: usize = 1_024;

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub(crate) struct MappingSet {
    pub(crate) format_version: u32,
    pub(crate) name: String,
    pub(crate) description: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) host: String,
    pub(crate) rules: Vec<Rule>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub(crate) struct Rule {
    pub(crate) method: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) subdomain: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) path: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) action_class: String,
}

/// Converts one TOML document to a checked mapping set. Errors carry the
/// set's declared name when the document parsed far enough to have one.
pub(crate) fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<MappingSet, (Option<String>, SetError)> {
    let set: MappingSet = toml::from_str(input).map_err(|error| (None, SetError::Toml(error)))?;
    match validate(&set) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(set),
        Err(error) => Err((Some(set.name), error)),
    }
}

fn validate(set: &MappingSet) -> Result<(), SetError> {
    if set.format_version != 1 {
        return Err(SetError::UnsupportedFormatVersion(set.format_version));
    }
    required_text("name", &set.name)?;
    if set
        .description
        .as_deref()
        .is_some_and(|description| description.chars().any(char::is_control))
    {
        return Err(SetError::InvalidField("description"));
    }
    validate_host(&set.host)?;
    if set.rules.is_empty() {
        return Err(SetError::InvalidField("rules"));
    }

    for (index, rule) in set.rules.iter().enumerate() {
        if !ACTION_CLASSES.contains(&rule.action_class.as_str()) {
            return Err(SetError::UnknownActionClass {
                rule: index,
                action_class: rule.action_class.clone(),
            });
        }
        if let Some(method) = &rule.method
            && normalize::method(method).is_none()
        {
            return Err(SetError::InvalidRule {
                rule: index,
                field: "method",
            });
        }
        if let Some(subdomain) = &rule.subdomain
            && subdomain != "*"
            && (!is_dns_name(subdomain) || normalize::host(subdomain).is_none())
        {
            return Err(SetError::InvalidRule {
                rule: index,
                field: "subdomain",
            });
        }
        if let Some(path) = &rule.path {
            let Some(normalized) = normalize::pattern_path(path) else {
                return Err(SetError::InvalidRule {
                    rule: index,
                    field: "path",
                });
            };
            if normalized.len() > MAX_PATTERN_BYTES {
                return Err(SetError::InvalidRule {
                    rule: index,
                    field: "path",
                });
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn required_text(field: &'static str, value: &str) -> Result<(), SetError> {
    if value.trim().is_empty() || value.chars().any(char::is_control) {
        Err(SetError::InvalidField(field))
    } else {
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn validate_host(host: &str) -> Result<(), SetError> {
    // Mapping hosts name an origin, not an HTTP authority. Ports and trailing
    // dots are accepted for request authorities but create duplicate mapping
    // identities, so reject them here.
    if !host.contains(':')
        && !host.ends_with('.')
        && normalize::host(host).is_some()
        && is_dns_name(host)
    {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(SetError::InvalidField("host"))
    }
}

fn is_dns_name(value: &str) -> bool {
    !value.is_empty() && value.len() <= 253 && value.split('.').all(is_dns_label)
}

fn is_dns_label(value: &str) -> bool {
    !value.is_empty()
        && value.len() <= 63
        && !value.starts_with('-')
        && !value.ends_with('-')
        && value
            .bytes()
            .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || byte == b'-')
}

//! Load-time conflict detection and set-order independence.

use action_classifier::{LoadError, RuleLocation, SetError, load};

fn set(name: &str, host: &str, rules: &str) -> String {
    format!("format_version = 1\nname = {name:?}\ndescription = \"test\"\nhost = {host:?}\n{rules}")
}

fn rule(subdomain: Option<&str>, method: Option<&str>, path: Option<&str>, class: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::from("\n[[rules]]\n");
    for (key, value) in [("subdomain", subdomain), ("method", method), ("path", path)] {
        if let Some(value) = value {
            out.push_str(&format!("{key} = {value:?}\n"));
        }
    }
    out.push_str(&format!("action_class = {class:?}\n"));
    out
}

fn location(set: usize, name: &str, rule: usize) -> RuleLocation {
    RuleLocation {
        set,
        name: name.into(),
        rule,
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn identical_rules_with_different_classes_conflict_across_sets() {
    let a = set(
        "A",
        "acme.com",
        &rule(
            Some("api"),
            Some("POST"),
            Some("/v1/refunds/*"),
            "payment.refund",
        ),
    );
    let b = set(
        "B",
        "acme.com",
        &format!(
            "{}{}",
            rule(None, None, Some("/pricing"), "payment.read"),
            rule(
                Some("api"),
                Some("POST"),
                Some("/v1/refunds/*"),
                "payment.read"
            ),
        ),
    );
    match load(&[&a, &b]).await {
        Err(LoadError::ConflictingRules { first, second }) => {
            assert_eq!(first, location(0, "A", 0));
            assert_eq!(second, location(1, "B", 1));
        }
        other => panic!("expected conflict, got {:?}", other.err()),
    }
}

# HARDENING.md — steering for the coding agent

Read this after `README.md`, `agents.md` and `Arch.md`. It turns the security
audit of `b2d8402` (see `backlog.md`) into ordered, bounded work items.

Precedence stays the same: README > fixed API > `agents.md` > `Arch.md` > this
file. If an item here conflicts with the README, stop and flag it.

## Ground rules

1. **Follow the design; only extend it where a defect was demonstrated.** Every
   item below either brings the code back in line with `Arch.md` (Tier 1), or
   adds to the design to close a reproduced problem (Tier 2/3). Do not
   restructure modules, add indexing, add dependencies, or "optimize" beyond
   what an item asks for. A linear scan is the accepted design (Arch §15).
2. **One item per commit.** Each commit contains the code change, a test that
   would have failed before it, and the matching `Arch.md` / `agents.md` edit.
   Code and docs must never disagree at any commit. The commit message names
   the item number (e.g. `H6: total conflict-analysis budget`).
3. **Never weaken a test to make it pass.** Never write a test that asserts the
   *less* sensitive class for an alternate spelling of a request. If a test
   seems wrong, stop and report rather than editing the expectation.
4. **Fail closed.** When unsure, the request is unclassified (`None`) or the
   config is rejected with an explicit `LoadError`. Never pick a class by
   guessing.
5. **Don't flip-flop on policy.** The policies in `Arch.md` §7/§9/§11 are
   decided. Do not revert method folding, `//` rejection, multi-label
   subdomains, or linear dot-segment removal.
6. **Same canonicalization both sides.** Any new path or host rule goes in the
   shared helpers in `normalize.rs` and applies to both config patterns and
   requests, unless the item says otherwise.
7. **Gates on every commit**, run from `Firma_take_home/`:
   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo build
   cargo test
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   ```
   The four tests in `tests/example.rs` must pass unchanged.
8. No `unwrap`/`expect` on untrusted input. `classify` must never panic. Keep
   `Classifier` `Send + Sync` and immutable after `load`.

## Work order

Do the items in this order. Stop after each tier and report.

---

## Tier 1 — make the code match the design

### H1. Check trailing slashes in one direction only (open HIGH, Audit 4/6)

- **Problem:** `classify` also checks `/x` against `/x/`. A narrower rule under
  a broader wildcard can never match: with `/v1/*/send` →
  `communication.external.send` and `/v1/*` → `payment.read`,
  `GET api.acme.com/v1/msg/send` returns `None`. This breaks README "the most
  specific wins".
- **Change (`src/lib.rs` `classify`):** only when the normalized path ends in
  `/` and isn't `/`, classify the path without that slash as well. Return
  `None` only if that result is `Some` and differs. A path without a trailing
  slash gets no alternate check.
- **Rationale for the doc:** the risk is a server stripping a trailing slash
  and running a more sensitive handler than the one classified. A request sent
  without the slash is already classified as sent.
- **Tests:**
  - `tests/classification.rs` `most_specific_rule_wins`: `/v1/msg/send` →
    `Some("communication.external.send")`.
  - `tests/security.rs`: `POST /v1/payouts` → `Some("payment.create")`, and
    `POST /v1/payouts/` → `None`.
  - Rename the security test to match the one-directional behaviour.
- **Docs:** Arch §9 and agents.md "Paths" say the check goes one way, with the
  rationale above.

### H2. Reject IP-like hosts (Arch §7, §9)

- **Problem:** only dotted-quad IPv4 is rejected. `010.0.0.1` and `127.1` load
  as config hosts and are accepted as request hosts.
- **Change (`normalize::host`):** reject any host whose last label is all
  digits. No real TLD is all-numeric (RFC 3696 §2). Config uses the same
  helper, so both sides are covered.
- **Tests:** a config `host` of `127.1` or `010.0.0.1` is rejected. A request
  host of `127.1`, `010.0.0.1` or `1.2.3.4.5` gives `None`.

### H3. Store the action class as `&'static str` (Arch §8)

- **Change:** `CompiledRule::action_class` holds the matching `ACTION_CLASSES`
  entry, found at compile time. An unknown class is a `CompileError`, which
  `load` maps to `SetError::UnknownActionClass`. `best_match` returns the
  stored reference.
- **Why:** only the seven classes can come back, guaranteed by the type rather
  than by validation order.

### H4. Make the robustness tests reach the matcher (Arch §17)

- **Problem:** the generator's alphabet doesn't contain `c`, `m` or `e`, so no
  generated host is ever under `acme.com`. Both tests only ever compare `None`
  with `None`.
- **Change (`tests/robustness.rs`):**
  - Pick the method from {`GET`, `POST`, `DELETE`, `get`, generated junk}.
  - Pick the host from {`api.acme.com`, `x.acme.com`, `a.b.acme.com`,
    `acme.com`, generated junk}.
  - Build the path from valid segments (`v1`, `refunds`, `x`, `.`, `..`,
    `%72efunds`, an empty last segment), then randomly mutate one byte.
- **Asserts:**
  - Results are deterministic and independent of set order.
  - Every result is `None` or a member of `ACTION_CLASSES`.
  - At least 25% of iterations classify to `Some`, so the test fails if the
    generator stops reaching the matcher again.
  - Use no new dependencies.

### H5. Test cleanups

- `tests/conflicts.rs` `same_class_duplicates_are_harmless`: change the path
  back from `/x*` to `/x`.
- `tests/security.rs` `method_case_does_not_fall_through_to_method_less_rule`:
  remove the standalone `DELETE` assertion that the loop already covers.
- `tests/conflicts.rs:165`: remove the stale "Exact subdomains are one DNS
  label" comment.
